title: People are quietly recording every conversation they have with AI, and the person across the table has no idea

content_html:
TL;DR

AI tools now record conversations without announcing themselves, and users are bringing them to dates and personal chats

A growing number of professionals have started using AI tools to record every conversation they have, and the people being recorded usually have no idea it is happening. The Wall Street Journal reported this week that apps like Granola, which transcribes meetings without deploying a visible bot or announcing its presence, have made ambient recording so frictionless that users are now bringing the technology out of conference rooms and into personal settings. The shift raises legal and ethical questions that neither the tools nor their users appear ready to answer.

Granola, which raised 125 million dollars earlier this year at a valuation of one and a half billion dollars, works by recording audio directly through the user’s device microphone rather than joining a call as a separate participant. That means no bot icon appears in the meeting and no automated message tells attendees they are being recorded. Michelle Lim, CEO of meeting software company Flint, told the Journal that she wishes Granola were running in every room she enters, a statement that captures both the appeal and the problem.

Some users have taken the concept well beyond the workplace, with Emmie Chang, founder of startup Yuzu Labs, telling the Journal she records first dates and sends the transcripts to Claude for feedback on how the conversation went. Others described recording therapy sessions, doctor visits, and casual dinners with friends, all without telling the other person. In the eleven US states that require all-party consent for recordings, including California, Florida, Illinois, and Pennsylvania, doing so without disclosure is a potential felony under state wiretapping laws.

The workplace implications are already materialising. Amy Dufrane, CEO of the Human Resource Certification Institute, told the Associated Press that AI note-takers pose enormous organisational risk, arguing that companies should not use them at all. Reports have surfaced of AI notetakers remaining on video calls after employees have left, silently documenting informal conversation and gossip, and privacy law expert Alex Alben warned that automatic recording involving third parties creates liability that most users have not considered.

Researchers have raised a separate concern that goes beyond privacy, with studies on cognitive offloading finding a negative correlation between heavy AI use and critical thinking. The worry is not just that people are recording without consent, but that they are losing the ability to listen, remember, and process conversations on their own. As these tools become cheaper and more invisible, the question is no longer whether they will spread but whether anyone will bother to ask permission first.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

人工智能工具现在可以在不通知自己的情况下记录对话，用户可以将它们带到约会和私人聊天中

越来越多的专业人士开始使用人工智能工具来记录他们的每一次对话，而被记录的人通常不知道它正在发生。 《华尔街日报》本周报道称，像 Granola 这样的应用程序可以在不部署可见机器人或宣布其存在的情况下转录会议，使环境录制变得如此顺畅，以至于用户现在将这项技术带出会议室并引入个人设置。 这种转变引发了法律和道德问题，这些工具及其用户似乎都没有准备好回答这些问题。

Granola 今年早些时候以 1.5 亿美元的估值筹集了 1.25 亿美元，其工作原理是直接通过用户设备的麦克风录制音频，而不是作为单独的参与者加入通话。 这意味着会议中不会出现机器人图标，也不会自动发送消息告诉与会者他们正在被录制。 会议软件公司 Flint 的首席执行官米歇尔·林 (Michelle Lim) 告诉《华尔街日报》，她希望她进入的每个房间都可以运行格兰诺拉麦片，这一声明既抓住了吸引力，也抓住了问题。

一些用户已经将这个概念带到了工作场所之外，初创公司 Yuzu Labs 的创始人 Emmie Chang 告诉《华尔街日报》，她记录了第一次约会，并将记录发送给克劳德，以获取有关谈话进行情况的反馈。 其他人则描述了记录治疗过程、看医生以及与朋友共进晚餐，所有这些都没有告诉对方。 在美国十一个要求录音需要各方同意的州，包括加利福尼亚州、佛罗里达州、伊利诺伊州和宾夕法尼亚州，根据州窃听法，在没有披露的情况下进行录音可能构成重罪。

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

对工作场所的影响已经显现。 人力资源认证研究所首席执行官艾米·杜弗兰 (Amy Dufrane) 告诉美联社，人工智能笔记员会带来巨大的组织风险，她认为公司根本不应该使用它们。 有报道称，人工智能记录员在员工离开后仍继续进行视频通话，默默记录非正式谈话和八卦，隐私法专家亚历克斯·阿尔本警告说，涉及第三方的自动录音会产生大多数用户没有考虑到的责任。

研究人员提出了一个超出隐私范围的单独担忧，对认知卸载的研究发现，人工智能的大量使用和批判性思维之间存在负相关。 令人担忧的不仅是人们在未经同意的情况下录音，还在于他们正在失去自己倾听、记忆和处理对话的能力。 随着这些工具变得更便宜、更隐形，问题不再是它们是否会传播，而是是否有人会先征求许可。
